data.funding_note:
FY2025 (10-K): AI/datacenter capex is overwhelmingly self-funded from operating cash flow. OCF was $136.2B vs. $64.55B "additions to property and equipment" (capex) — MSFT does NOT break out a separate "AI capex" line, but states capex is "to support growth in our cloud offerings and our investments in AI infrastructure and training." Total bond debt actually DECLINED to $43.15B (FY25) from $44.94B (FY24), and net financing was a cash OUTFLOW (repayments exceeded issuance). So the on-balance-sheet bond stack is not funding AI — OCF is.

HOWEVER, the bear-relevant nuance is OFF-the-cash-flow-statement datacenter financing via FINANCE LEASES and build-to-suit / not-yet-commenced leases, which is exploding:
- Total finance lease liabilities (primarily datacenters): $46.17B at FY25-end, up from $27.15B a year earlier; finance-lease ROU assets obtained in FY25 = $20.5B (on top of $64.55B cash capex). By Q3 FY26 (2026-03-31) total finance lease liabilities reached $62.93B; finance-lease P&E at cost reached $77.6B.
- Leases that had NOT YET COMMENCED, "primarily for datacenters": $92.7B at FY25-end, then $196.6B at 2026-03-31 — i.e. roughly doubling in nine months, commencing FY2026–FY2031. This is the build-to-suit/SPV-style datacenter financing pipeline and is the fastest-growing AI-infrastructure obligation; it is contractual but not yet on the balance sheet.
- FY25 contractual obligations: construction commitments $32.1B (primarily datacenters); operating+finance leases incl. imputed interest $178.7B; purchase commitments $109.95B that "primarily relate to datacenters and include open purchase orders and take-or-pay contracts."

Updated demand-strength signal (Q3 FY26 10-Q): commercial remaining performance obligation (RPO) jumped 99% YoY to $627B (total RPO $633B), and 9-month FY26 OCF rose to $127.5B while 9-month capex rose to $80.1B (Q3 alone $30.9B) — capex acceleration is being matched by OCF and a record contracted-revenue backlog, supporting the self-funding (rational-growth) read rather than the leverage (bubble) read. Caveat: cash+short-term investments fell to $78.3B (from $94.6B) as capex outran even rising OCF, and the $196.6B not-yet-commenced datacenter-lease pipeline is the principal vector by which MSFT's AI buildout is being financed off the income/cash-flow statement.

NEOCLOUD/COREWEAVE/OPENAI: MSFT's 10-K and 10-Qs contain NO named take-or-pay or RPO commitment to CoreWeave, Nebius, or other neoclouds (no such names appear in the filings). MSFT's only related AI-investee disclosure is OpenAI as an equity-method investment (net recognized losses on equity method investments "including OpenAI"); no dollar commitment figure is disclosed. Any MSFT→neocloud compute purchases would be inside the undifferentiated $109.95B "purchase commitments (primarily datacenters, incl. take-or-pay)" line and are not separately quantified. classify: funding_source = predominantly_operating_cash_flow, with a rising and material finance-lease / not-yet-commenced-lease financing overlay that is the key item to watch.

data.funding_note: Demand-side verdict: Alphabet's AI/data-center capex is predominantly self-funded by operating cash flow, but 2025 saw a material, deliberate layering of leverage and off-balance-sheet data-center financing on top. Capex of $91.4B (FY2025, +74% from $52.5B FY2024) is covered ~1.8x by $164.7B operating cash flow; even adding $45.4B buybacks + $10.0B dividends, OCF nearly covers all uses. The 10-K explicitly ties the capex surge to AI ('we continue to invest in capital expenditures as we scale our technical infrastructure, in particular for AI') and guides that in 2026 it will 'significantly increase, relative to 2025' its technical-infrastructure investment (no dollar figure given in 10-K). LEVERAGE SIGNAL (the bubble-watch flag): long-term debt grew 4.3x from $10.9B to $46.5B; total senior unsecured notes carrying value $48.5B (vs $11.9B in 2024); Alphabet issued $22.5B USD + EUR13.25B notes in 2025 ($37.3B net proceeds) 'for general corporate purposes' (NOT earmarked to AI). Beyond on-balance-sheet debt, the financed-infrastructure exposure is larger: $58.5B of data-center leases NOT YET COMMENCED ($5.8B short-term + $52.7B long-term, off-balance-sheet, commencing 2026-2031), finance lease liabilities of $2.5B (up from $1.7B, 'primarily for data centers'), data-center leasing VIEs accounted for as finance leases, plus 2025 credit support/backstops/guarantees to infrastructure counterparties accounted for as credit derivatives. The ai_related_debt_or_financing figure (~$61B) is an analyst aggregation of finance-lease liabilities ($2.5B) + uncommenced data-center leases ($58.5B); the $48.5B of senior notes is general-corporate and is reported separately as total_debt. Purchase commitments & other contractual obligations total $149.1B, of which $113.0B short-term 'mostly related to technical infrastructure and inventory orders' (i.e., servers/compute + energy take-or-pay) — this is the demand commitment that is the financed core's revenue. NO neocloud/CoreWeave/Nebius/Crusoe/Lambda compute-purchase or take-or-pay commitments appear in Alphabet's 10-K: Google is a hyperscaler (supply side), not a neocloud customer; compute_purchase_commitments to neoclouds = unfound for Alphabet. Net: rational self-funding core, but 2025 marks a clear pivot to debt + off-balance-sheet lease financing around the AI build-out, hence mixed rather than predominantly operating-cash-flow.

data.funding_note: DIRECTIONAL NOTE: Amazon is NOT a demand-side neocloud customer -- it IS a hyperscaler/AI compute SUPPLIER. The relevant neocloud-style commitment runs the OTHER way: AWS holds a $38.0B multi-year commercial commitment with OpenAI, EXPANDED by $100.0B over 8 years in Q1 2026 (incl. AWS chips) -- this is revenue TO Amazon from the financed AI core (OpenAI), not Amazon's spend. Amazon also holds equity in Anthropic ($45.8B convertible notes + ~$14.8B preferred at Dec-2025) and OpenAI ($15.0B invested Q1 2026 + $35.0B equity commitment through Dec-2028). FUNDING THESIS: Through FY2025 the AI/datacenter capex was self-funding from operating cash flow -- OCF $139.5B vs net capex $128.3B left positive free cash flow of $11.2B; financing was a net +$9.7B but Amazon ended 2025 with only $68.8B face-value debt against $123.0B cash+investments (net cash positive). This was the RATIONAL/self-funding profile. However the inflection is decisive in the most recent data: TTM ended Mar-31-2026 OCF $148.5B vs net capex $147.3B drove free cash flow to just $1.2B (down from $25.9B a year earlier) -- capex now consumes essentially ALL operating cash flow. Concurrently, in March 2026 alone Amazon issued ~$53.8B of new unsecured senior notes (face-value debt jumped from $68.8B at Dec-2025 to $122.6B at Mar-2026; long-term debt on balance sheet $65.6B -> $119.1B), and Q1 2026 cash capex was $43.2B (vs $24.3B Q1 2025), guided to increase further in 2026. So the marginal funding of the AI build-out has shifted from pure operating cash flow toward debt/financing -- hence MIXED. Total debt figure reported is FY2025 face value ($68.8B); ai_related_debt_or_financing captures the ~$53.8B March-2026 senior-note raise that funded the accelerating datacenter capex. Finance leases ($12.3B PV) and build-to-suit/SPV financing obligations (~$8.1B, data-center & fulfillment) are additional off-revolver datacenter financing. No CoreWeave/neocloud purchase commitments by Amazon (none disclosed; not applicable to a supplier).

verdict.note: All cited figures independently verified against both filings in-repo (10-K amzn-20251231.htm; 10-Q amzn-20260331.htm). FY2025 self-funding confirmed: OCF $139,514M minus net capex $128,320M = FCF +$11,194M (matches filing reconciliation exactly), and cash+investments $123,029M ($86,810M cash + $36,219M securities) vs face-value debt $68,836M = net cash positive (+$54.2B). So FY2025 cash flow DOES cover capex; no debt needed. The 'mixed' classification rests on the disclosed post-period inflection: TTM ended Mar-31-2026 OCF $148,531M minus net capex $147,299M = FCF +$1,232M (down from $25,925M a year prior) -- capex now consumes ~99% of OCF -- concurrent with a ~$53.8B March-2026 senior-note raise (EUR 14.5B/$16.8B + $37.0B), which reconciles exactly to the total-face-value debt jump $68,836M -> $122,632M (+$53,796M). funding_source 'mixed_cash_and_debt' is source-backed and the funding_note transparently flags the period mismatch (total_debt is FY2025; ai_related_debt is the Mar-2026 raise). data.funding_note: NVIDIA is the SUPPLY side of the AI/data-center trade, not a demand-side buildout entity, so classic "demand-side capex funded by debt" framing largely does not apply. Its own capex is tiny relative to scale: FY2026 cash purchases of property, equipment and intangible assets were just $6.0B against $102.7B of operating cash flow (capex is ~6% of OCF). NVDA is fabless; it has no large self-built data-center PP&E program. Funding is overwhelmingly operating cash flow: it ended FY2026 with $62.6B cash+marketable securities and only $8.5B of fixed-rate senior Notes (net carrying $8,468M, of which $999M short-term); commercial paper program was expanded in Jan 2026 from $575M to $25.0B but ZERO was outstanding. Finance leases are immaterial (combined leasehold-improvement + finance-lease accumulated amortization only $519M). There is NO AI/data-center-specific debt, no build-to-suit/SPV data-center financing, and no finance-lease-funded compute. Critically for the bubble thesis, NVDA discloses it has 'been asked to offer financing arrangements to support our customers' and partners' buildout of datacenter infrastructure' but states flatly: 'We have not entered into any financing arrangements' (i.e., it is NOT, as of this 10-K, vendor-financing the neoclouds on-balance-sheet). On the commitment side, the figures that matter are: (a) $95.2B of manufacturing/supply/capacity purchase commitments (to TSMC etc., demand-side supply chain, substantially all payable through FY2027); (b) $27B of multi-year cloud service agreement commitments — this is NVDA itself buying back compute capacity from CSPs/neoclouds (e.g. CoreWeave-type capacity, for R&D), payable $7B/$6B/$5B/$5B/$2B/$2B across FY2027-FY2032+; this is the take-or-pay leg where NVDA's own cash flow underwrites a financed neocloud's revenue; (c) $11.4B investment commitments and $3.4B other. CoreWeave is not named in NVDA's own 10-K (counterparties not disclosed by name). Bottom line: on its own books NVDA's AI capex is rational, trivially self-funded from operating cash flow with negligible leverage; the leverage/bubble risk sits with its customers/neoclouds, to whom NVDA is exposed via $27B+ of multi-year cloud commitments and supply-chain take-or-pay, not via its own financing.

What IS disclosed in counterparties' filings is the demand-side core: OpenAI's take-or-pay compute purchase commitments to neocloud CoreWeave. CoreWeave's FY2025 10-K and Q1 2026 10-Q disclose OpenAI commitments of (a) ~$11.9B through October 2030 (March 2025 MSA) and (b) up to ~$6.5B through May 31, 2031 (May 2025 MSA / September 2025 order form) — at least ~$18.4B of disclosed contracted compute spend (the widely-reported aggregate including a May 2025 ~$4B expansion is ~$22.4B, but only the $11.9B and $6.5B tranches are explicitly quantified in these filings; the $4B expansion is not separately quantified here so is excluded from the cited sum). CLASSIFICATION (predominantly_debt_or_financing): the demand OpenAI represents is being met through debt-financed, off-OpenAI-balance-sheet infrastructure (neocloud leverage), not visibly from OpenAI operating cash flow; OpenAI is loss-making and its compute obligations are take-or-pay liabilities backstopping >$20B of CoreWeave borrowing. Separately, Microsoft's Q1 2026 10-Q discloses a ~27% as-converted equity-method stake in OpenAI (post-October-2025 recapitalization) and net equity-method losses/gains from OpenAI ($5.9B net gain for the nine months ended Mar 31, 2026, primarily a recapitalization dilution gain) — confirming OpenAI's reliance on external equity/strategic financing rather than self-funding. The $20B 'ai_related_debt_or_financing' figure is CoreWeave's customer-contract-driven financing (a proxy for the debt funding OpenAI's demand), NOT OpenAI's own debt, which is unfound.

verdict.entity: OpenAI (OpenAI OpCo, LLC / OpenAI Global, LLC) — private; figures from counterparty SEC filings
verdict.note: Demand-side figures are source-backed and the unfound flags are honest. Arithmetic verified: $11.9B (Mar 2025 MSA, through Oct 2030) + $6.5B (May 2025 MSA/Sept 2025 order form, through May 31 2031) = exactly $18.4B; both tranches are explicitly quantified in the cited CoreWeave 10-K quote. The ~$4B expansion to reach the reported ~$22.4B aggregate is correctly excluded as unquantified in these filings. RPO progression ($15.1B Dec-2024 -> $60.7B Dec-2025 -> $98.8B Mar-2026) is internally consistent across the two CoreWeave filings; no unit/period errors found (all USD billions; FY2025 10-K = YE Dec-31-2025, Q1 2026 10-Qs = period ended Mar-31-2026). CAPEX vs OPERATING CASH FLOW: cannot be assessed for OpenAI directly — OpenAI is private and files no SEC reports, so its own capex, operating cash flow, cash, and debt are all correctly null/unfound and not fabricated. The data does not claim OpenAI cash flow covers capex; it argues (with support) that demand is met via debt-financed, off-OpenAI-balance-sheet neocloud infrastructure. The CoreWeave DDTL 5.0 quote ('entered into primarily to finance capital expenditures required to perform certain customer contracts') and the '>$20 billion of debt and equity capital year-to-date' line directly tie the customer-contract (incl. OpenAI take-or-pay) capex to debt — so cash flow does NOT cover this capex; debt is needed. FUNDING_SOURCE CLASSIFICATION (predominantly_debt_or_financing): supported only for the COUNTERPARTY/PROXY funding (CoreWeave's debt financing the OpenAI-contracted compute), which IS independently supported by the cited DDTL filings. It is NOT confirmed for OpenAI's own funding, which is unfound — hence funding_source_confirmed=false. Minor caveat: the $20B ai_related_debt_or_financing figure is '>$20B of debt AND equity'; the actually-quantified DEBT portion is $8.5B DDTL 4.0 + $3.1B DDTL 5.0 = $11.6B. The note transparently labels the $20B a proxy and 'NOT OpenAI's own debt,' so it is not misleading, but the field name 'debt_or_financing' is doing the work of folding equity in. Microsoft's ~27% as-converted equity-method stake and the $5.9B nine-month net gain ('primarily the dilution gain from the OpenAI Recapitalization,' vs prior-year net losses) corroborate OpenAI being loss-making/externally funded. Verdict: source_backed for the demand-side core and the financed-core proxy; funding_source_confirmed=false because OpenAI's own capex/cash-flow/debt mix is genuinely unfound from primary SEC sources and the classification rests on counterparty inference, not direct OpenAI disclosure.
corrections: ai_related_debt_or_financing_usd ($20B) cites '>$20 billion of debt AND equity capital' — it is not purely debt; the SEC-quantified pure-debt portion is $8.5B DDTL 4.0 + $3.1B DDTL 5.0 = $11.6B. Consider relabeling the $20B as 'debt+equity capital raised' to avoid implying it is all debt.

funding_source classification is supported for CoreWeave (the proxy/financed core) but not for OpenAI's own balance sheet; the classification should be explicitly scoped as a counterparty-inferred proxy, since OpenAI's own funding source is unfound.
